descriptionChirho: The physical lip(s) of a person, used literally for the organ of speech or in expressions involving lips (covering, opening, flattering, guarding, etc.); Arabic شَفَة/شَفَتَيْنِ, Korean 입술, Swahili midomo.
Human language or tongue as a system of communication, especially in the Babel narrative (Gen 11:1,6-7,9) and references to foreign/unintelligible speech; Arabic لُغَة, Korean 언어, Swahili lugha.

The rim, brim, or border of a manufactured object such as a vessel, curtain, garment, or basin (e.g., the molten sea in 1 Kgs 7, tabernacle curtains in Exod 26); Arabic حَافَة/حَاشِيَة, Korean 가장자리, Swahili ukingo.

The shore or bank of a body of water (sea, river, stream), often in narrative descriptions of geography or divine promises (Gen 22:17, 41:3, Exod 7:15, etc.); Arabic شَاطِئ/ضِفَّة, Korean 해변/기슭, Swahili ukingo/ufuo.
Speech or utterance as a metonymic extension from lip, referring to what is spoken rather than the physical organ; Arabic الكَلَام, Korean 말, Swahili usemi.
